_what: Static picture formats as data — the SHAPE a still ad takes, independent of brand, angle and product. The copy banks cover the words; this covers the picture.
_sources: Two paid advertisers only, both selling to women past fifty: <competitor> and <competitor B>. Nothing here is derived from our own past drops.
_sampling: <competitor>: 216 distinct statics, 53 sampled across all 11 copy blocks. <competitor B>: 99 statics across 72 angle folders, science and clearance blocks read in full. Counts are of the SAMPLE and are a floor, not a total.
_provenance_rule: duplicated = the same shape rebuilt N times in one advertiser's live set. Nobody re-executes a shape that is not working, so repetition is a spend decision someone else already paid for. observed = seen once or twice; kept so it is not rediscovered.
_native_crossover: Rows flagged native_crossover borrow the look of organic content rather than advertising. These are the bridge to the native-static play: an ad shaped like what she already scrolls, carrying long-form copy underneath that reads as the post continuing.

formats.name: Handwritten note, held
formats.what: A hand holds a small handwritten note to camera beside the product, shallow focus, real surface. The claim is entirely in the handwriting.
formats.why_it_works: Handwriting reads as a person, not a brand, so the claim lands before the defence goes up. Cheapest shape in the bank — no model, no studio, no retouching.
formats.evidence: duplicated ×4 in the sample, across two different copy blocks
formats.source: components/swipe-paid/competitor/_raw (216 distinct statics, 53 sampled across all 11 copy blocks)
examples: Turns out my 'tired face' was just skin waiting for peptides.
No needles. No freezing my face. Just this.
My eye bags packed up and left.
carries: a rejection of the expensive alternative

formats.name: UGC post, screenshotted
formats.what: A real woman at her mirror or holding her phone, shot as if it were her own post, with review cards or step panels laid over it. Often framed as a phone screen.
formats.why_it_works: It is the closest thing in the paid set to what she already scrolls. The ad borrows the shape of organic content rather than interrupting it.
formats.source: components/swipe-paid/competitor/_raw (216 distinct statics, 53 sampled across all 11 copy blocks)
examples: How I get even skin in 1 min
grwm: the foundation that finds my shade

formats.name: Struck price
formats.what: Old price struck through, new price beside it, usually circled or in a pill. Product and little else.
formats.why_it_works: Does one job with no argument at all, which is why it survives being run at volume alongside everything else.
formats.evidence: duplicated ×6 in the sample — the most repeated treatment overall, though it is an offer shape not an argument shape
formats.source: components/swipe-paid/competitor/_raw (216 distinct statics, 53 sampled across all 11 copy blocks)

formats.name: Split with data labels
formats.what: Two macro images side by side, each with one hard label in a black pill — a number, a name, a state. No sentence.
formats.why_it_works: Asserts a difference without claiming a result, so it reads as information rather than advertising and survives review.
formats.evidence: duplicated ×3 in the <competitor B> science block
formats.source: components/swipe-paid/capture/assets/competitor-b/by-angle (99 statics across 72 angles)
examples: 50,000+ DALTONS | 240 DALTONS

formats.name: Red-circle annotation
formats.what: A photograph with a hand-drawn red ellipse around the thing being pointed at, usually with a short pointer label.
formats.why_it_works: The most recognisable 'look here' mark there is, borrowed from evidence rather than advertising.
formats.evidence: duplicated across BOTH advertisers — 4+ in the <competitor B> science block, plus before/after use in <competitor>
formats.source: both
formats.note: A device more than a format — it composes onto a split, a scan, a chart or a face.

formats.name: Phone notes list
formats.what: A screenshot of the notes app: lowercase title, then five or six em-dash lines. No photography at all.
formats.why_it_works: Reads as something she wrote for herself. A list carries six objections in one ad without feeling like a feature list.
formats.source: components/swipe-paid/competitor/_raw (216 distinct statics, 53 sampled across all 11 copy blocks)
examples: note to self — your daughter was right about the foundation
things I stopped doing since switching foundations
carries: an accumulated list of failed fixes

formats.name: Hand-annotated product
formats.what: The product on a plain ground with pencil arrows and handwritten notes pointing at parts of it.
formats.why_it_works: Same trick as the sticky note at spec-sheet scale — handwriting makes a claim list feel like a person explaining rather than a brand listing.
formats.source: components/swipe-paid/competitor/_raw (216 distinct statics, 53 sampled across all 11 copy blocks)
examples: one shade, fair to medium
money-back if it doesn't match
carries: the whole offer in one frame

formats.name: Annotated diagram
formats.what: A medical or technical illustration with leader lines to labelled parts, in textbook language rather than brand language.
formats.why_it_works: Borrows the authority of the reference book, and carries a mechanism with no person in frame — so no casting problem.
formats.evidence: duplicated ×2, plus near-relatives (histology grid, molecular render) in the same block
formats.source: components/swipe-paid/capture/assets/competitor-b/by-angle (99 statics across 72 angles)
examples: YOUTHFUL FACE | AGING FACE, eleven labelled callouts

formats.name: Editorial page
